ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a circular maze, with black curves and radial line segments forming walls, and the white regions are passable corridors. Point O is located near the center, A is in the lower-left outer passage, B is in the lower-right outer passage, C is in the upper outer passage, D is in the middle-level passage slightly left of the bottom, and E is in the lower-right inner passage. Reasoning: According to the method of the problem, treat the black lines as walls that cannot be crossed, and starting from O, one can only move along connected white regions. Observing the white passage near O, one can go around the inner wall upward and leftward into the upper annular corridor, and continue through the upper opening to reach the region marked C. Then check the other points: the regions where A, B, D, and E are located are all separated from the connected region where O is located by black arcs or radial walls, and cannot be reached directly through white passages. Therefore, the marked point reachable from O is C.

method.method_draft: Treat the black curves and radial segments in the image as walls and the white regions as passable corridors. Starting from the dot labeled O near the center, visually trace only through connected white space, marking walls as barriers. From O, follow the open passage upward/leftward around the inner wall, then outward through the visible gap into the upper annular corridor. Continue along this connected corridor to the upper region where point C lies. Check the other labeled points A, B, D, and E: each is separated from O's connected corridor by at least one black wall segment. Therefore the reachable labeled point is C.
